newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania president presses on war crimes case.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania president presses on war crimes case.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas on Thursday urged prosecutors to speed up their investigation into the case of a Lithuanian accused of playing a key role in the wartime massacre of the country's Jews.
Alexander Lileikis, 90, is accused of having handed Jews over to Nazi death squads in Vilnius during World War Two when he was head of the local security police under German occupation.
Lithuania has been under pressure to prosecute Lileikis and other alleged war criminals. The Israeli Knesset recently sent a letter to Brazauskas urging him to get the case against Lileikis moving.
"The president suggested to the prosecutor's office to speed up its investigation of the Alexander Lileikis case and to take it to court," the president's office said in a statement.
Lileikis returned to Lithuania last June after being stripped of his U.S. citizenship on the grounds he lied about his wartime activities.
Lileikis, who has been questioned several times by Lithuanian prosecutors as a witness, has protested his innocence and claimed that his activities were innocuous.

He is one of several Lithuanians targeted by Nazi hunters for their alleged role in the Holocaust, which historians say claimed the lives of 94 percent of Lithuania's pre-war Jewish population of 220,000.
There are currently five Lithuanians living in their homeland who have lost their American citizenship and U.S. prosecutors are building cases against several more.
Lithuania has been accused of dragging its feet over the issue but prosecutors here say building watertight cases five decades after the crime is a difficult task.
